greek.civilizationInsight: Western civilization built on discourse - speaking before being. The word as an external instrument of power.

derivations: phýō - to grow, to be born
greek.civilizationInsight: Greek civilization focused on physis as the process of coming-to-be, contrasted with dharmic civilization's focus on dhāraṇa (holding).

hebrew.meaning: to create from nothing, shape, fashion
hebrew.civilizationInsight: Abrahamic civilization: creation as ex nihilo, divine creator vs. human creation. Bara places a gap between creator and created.

derivations: davar - divine word has material creative force
hebrew.civilizationInsight: Hebrew: the divine word is material. When prophet speaks, word commands. Contrast with mantra - transforms consciousness through sound.

arabic.meaning: to know, to teach, to learn
arabic.civilizationInsight: Arabic: knowledge transmission through formalized teaching (ʿallama) and learning (taʿallama). Knowledge as acquisition through structured pedagogy.

derivations: dao - the eternal way that cannot be named
dao - to guide, to show the way
chinese.civilizationInsight: Chinese: Dao is ineffable. The Way that can be named is not the eternal Way. Chinese civilization built around a concept declaring its own linguistic inadequacy.

derivations: de - inherent force and power that moves the world
de - moral virtue, psychic quality of the king
chinese.civilizationInsight: Chinese: De as both moral virtue and psychic life force. The Dao de jing shows de as activation of dao in the visible world.

Shrikant Talageri: 'The Puru-Bharata lineage - Pūru purifier, Bharata bearer.'
